shared_elements: upright pale limestone slab/pillar set in ground
loose stone rubble at the base
weathered/eroded stone surface with faint relief traces
vertical edge dividing the block from surrounding matrix
justification: Both show a tall pale limestone block standing in an excavated context with rubble heaped at its foot, and in each the stone surface bears shallow, weather-blurred modelling, which gives a faint material and framing resemblance. The decisive difference is that B carries a legible, ordered programme of relief imagery (a top register of repeated arched motifs, a fringe-like band, birds, a disc, quadrupeds and long-necked creatures stacked in registers), whereas A presents no identifiable figures at all, only erosion patterns and cracks, so no shared iconography or compositional scheme can honestly be asserted.
